checks.title: go.mod and go.sum are both committed
checks.why: Without go.sum in version control the build trusts whatever the module proxy returns that day, so a dependency can change under you between two builds of the same commit.
checks.action: Commit go.mod and go.sum together. Never add go.sum to gitignore, and never regenerate it as part of the deploy.

verify.expect: Both files are listed. If go.sum is missing the build has no checksum to verify against.

checks.title: The Go version is pinned, not whatever the machine has
checks.why: A build that takes the toolchain it happens to find changes compiler behaviour and standard library patches between deploys, which turns a bug into one that only appears on one machine.
checks.action: Name a version in the go directive, and build with that same version in CI and in the release image.

verify.expect: A go directive names an explicit version, and the build environment uses the same one.

checks.title: Known vulnerabilities in dependencies have been reviewed
checks.why: The module graph of a normal service pulls in dozens of packages, and a known vulnerable version can sit there for months without anything failing.
checks.action: Run the vulnerability scanner before a release and decide on each finding. It reports only vulnerabilities in code paths your program actually reaches, so the list is usually short.

verify.expect: No unreviewed finding. Each one is either fixed by an upgrade or recorded with a reason it does not apply.

checks.title: Release binaries are built with trimpath
checks.why: Without it the binary embeds the absolute path of every source file, which hands out the build machine layout, the CI directory structure and often a username.
checks.action: Pass trimpath to the release build so recorded paths become module paths instead of local ones. It also makes the build reproducible across machines.

verify.expect: The release build path passes trimpath. A local development build does not need it.

checks.title: The shipped binary was not built with the race detector
checks.why: A race build runs several times slower and uses far more memory. It is easy to leave the flag in a Makefile target that both the test job and the release job call.
checks.action: Keep the race flag on the test target only. Check that the release target, the container build and any goreleaser configuration do not inherit it.

verify.expect: Every hit belongs to a test or CI job, and none is on the path that produces the artifact you deploy.

checks.title: GOMAXPROCS reflects the container CPU limit
checks.why: In a container with a CPU quota the runtime still sees every core on the host, so it runs far more scheduler threads than the quota allows and the program spends its time being throttled.
checks.action: Set GOMAXPROCS from the quota in the deployment, or have the program read the cgroup limit at startup and set it.

verify.manual: Look at the deployment for a CPU limit. If one is set, confirm that either the environment sets GOMAXPROCS to match or the program adjusts it at startup.

checks.title: The binary can say which commit it came from
checks.why: When something misbehaves in production, the first question is which build is running. An unstamped binary cannot answer it, and the deploy log is not always trustworthy by then.
checks.action: Stamp the commit and version at build time, either through the module build information Go records automatically or through linker flags, and expose it in a startup log line or a version flag.

verify.expect: The output names a version and a revision rather than devel or an empty value.

checks.title: The cgo setting matches the image the binary runs in
checks.why: With cgo on, the binary links against the host C library. Copied into a scratch or distroless image it fails at startup with a missing loader, and the error names a file rather than the cause.
checks.action: Build with cgo disabled for a static binary, or use a base image that carries the C library the binary was linked against. Decide which, rather than inheriting the default.

verify.manual: Check the base image in the Dockerfile against the cgo setting used for the build. A scratch or distroless image needs a static binary.
